title: Reproduction
subtitle: One parent makes a copy. Two parents make something new.
objectives: Explain the difference between asexual and sexual reproduction
Name four modes of asexual reproduction in animals and plants
Name the parts of a flower and what each does
Explain pollination and fertilisation in plants
Distinguish oviparous, viviparous and ovoviviparous animals

cards.title: Some living things do not need a partner at all
cards.text: One organism, no mate, and the offspring is an exact copy. It is fast, it is cheap, and it has one serious weakness.

cards.title: Asexual reproduction
cards.text: One parent. The offspring gets an identical copy of the parent's genetic information.
points: **No partner needed**, so no time is wasted finding one.
**Every offspring is a clone.**
**Very fast.** A bacterium can divide in twenty minutes.
**Zero variation.** That is the weakness.

cards.title: Four ways to do it without a partner
cards.text: These are the four the exam asks for, and each one is a different physical process.
points: **Binary fission** — split in two. Amoeba, bacteria.
**Budding** — a bump grows and breaks off. Hydra, yeast.
**Fragmentation** — a broken piece regrows whole. Starfish.
**Parthenogenesis** — an egg develops with no fertilisation.

question.text: Which is a form of asexual reproduction?
question.explain: Budding needs one parent only. The other three all involve two sets of genetic information.

cards.title: Vegetative propagation
cards.text: A whole new plant grows from a root, a stem or a leaf. No seed, no flower, no pollen.
points: **Runners** — strawberry plants send them sideways.
**Tubers** — a potato's eyes are new plants.
**Bulbs** — onions and garlic.
**Cuttings and grafting** — the gardener's version.

cards.title: Copy-paste against a random seed
cards.text: Asexual reproduction is duplicating a build. Sexual reproduction is generating a new world from a seed you did not choose.
points: **Copy** — identical, fast, predictable.
**Seed** — different every time, and sometimes better.
**One is safe until conditions change.**
**The other is slower and adapts.**

question.text: A potato grows new plants from its eyes. What is this called?
question.explain: Vegetative propagation — a new plant from a stem, root or leaf, with no seed involved.

cards.title: Identical units share identical faults
cards.text: When a factory builds ten thousand identical cars and one part is wrong, all ten thousand have it. Clones work the same way.
points: **That is what a recall is.**
**One disease that beats one clone** beats all of them.
**Variation is insurance**, not decoration.
**This is why sexual reproduction survives** despite the cost.

cards.title: Good spot to pause
cards.text: One parent done. Part 2 is two parents, and the flower that manages it without moving. Your place is saved.

cards.title: A flower is a reproductive organ that cannot move
cards.text: It has to get pollen to another plant without going anywhere. Everything about a flower is a solution to that problem.

cards.title: Six parts, cut in half
cards.text: Tap each one. Two quiz questions come straight from this.

question.text: Which part of a flower makes pollen?
question.explain: The anther, on top of the filament. Together they make the stamen, the male part.

cards.title: Pollination is not fertilisation
cards.text: These are two separate events and the exam checks whether you know that. One is a journey. The other is a joining.
points: **Pollination** — pollen lands on a stigma.
**Fertilisation** — the pollen nucleus joins the ovule.
**A pollen tube grows down the style** in between.
**Ovules become seeds. The ovary becomes fruit.**

cards.title: Three words for how the young arrive
cards.text: All three are sexual reproduction. The difference is only where the embryo develops.
points: **Oviparous** — lays eggs. Birds, most fish, reptiles.
**Viviparous** — live young. Most mammals.
**Ovoviviparous** — eggs hatch inside the mother.
***Ovi* means egg. *Vivi* means alive.**

question.text: What is the difference between pollination and fertilisation?
options: Pollination is pollen landing; fertilisation is the joining of nuclei
They are two words for the same event
question.explain: A journey, then a joining. The pollen tube grows down the style between the two.

cards.title: Why nobody is a copy of a parent
cards.text: You got half your genetic information from each parent, shuffled. That is why siblings differ, and why you are not either of them.
points: **Half and half**, and never the same half twice.
**That shuffle is the whole point** of two parents.
**Variation is what lets a species adapt.**
**A clone population cannot.**

question.text: Asexual reproduction produces offspring with variation.
question.explain: False. The offspring are clones. Variation is the thing sexual reproduction buys, at the cost of needing a partner.

terms.def: One parent, and offspring that are genetic copies.
Two parents, gametes, and offspring with new combinations.
One cell splits into two. Amoeba and bacteria.
A bump grows on the parent and breaks off. Hydra and yeast.
A broken piece regrows into a whole organism. Starfish.
A new plant from a root, stem or leaf. Runners, tubers, bulbs, cuttings.
The male part of a flower: filament plus anther.
The female part: stigma, style and ovary.
Pollen landing on a stigma. A journey, not a joining.
The pollen nucleus joining the ovule. This is when a seed begins.
Gives birth to live young. Vivi- means alive.

cards.title: The four that matter
points: **One parent = clones. Two parents = variation.**
**Fission, budding, fragmentation, propagation.**
**Anther makes pollen. Stigma receives it.**
**Pollination is the journey. Fertilisation is the joining.**

quiz.text: What is the main difference between asexual and sexual reproduction?
options: Asexual needs one parent and gives clones; sexual needs two and gives variation
Asexual reproduction happens only in water
quiz.explain: One parent against two, and copies against new combinations. Everything else follows from that.
quiz.objective: Explain the difference between asexual and sexual reproduction

quiz.text: An amoeba splits into two. What is this called?
quiz.explain: Binary fission — one cell divides into two identical cells.
quiz.objective: Name four modes of asexual reproduction in animals and plants

quiz.text: A hydra grows a bump that breaks off as a new individual. What is this?
quiz.explain: Budding. Yeast does the same thing.
quiz.objective: Name four modes of asexual reproduction in animals and plants

quiz.text: Which of these is vegetative propagation?
options: A strawberry plant sending out a runner
quiz.explain: A new plant from a stem, with no seed involved. Tubers, bulbs and cuttings are the same idea.
quiz.objective: Name four modes of asexual reproduction in animals and plants

quiz.text: Which part of the flower makes pollen?
quiz.explain: The anther, sitting on the filament. Together they are the stamen.
quiz.objective: Name the parts of a flower and what each does

quiz.text: Which part of the flower receives pollen?
quiz.explain: The stigma, the sticky pad on top of the style. Nothing happens until pollen lands there.
quiz.objective: Name the parts of a flower and what each does

quiz.text: What does the ovary become after fertilisation?
quiz.explain: The ovary becomes the fruit and the ovules inside it become the seeds.
quiz.objective: Explain pollination and fertilisation in plants

quiz.text: Put these in order, from first to last.
items: A pollen tube grows down the style
quiz.explain: Pollination, then the tube, then fertilisation, then the seed. Four separate steps.
quiz.objective: Explain pollination and fertilisation in plants

quiz.explain: Ovi- means egg. Vivi- means alive, so viviparous is live young.
quiz.objective: Distinguish oviparous, viviparous and ovoviviparous animals

quiz.text: In an ovoviviparous animal, where do the eggs hatch?
quiz.explain: Inside the mother, so live young emerge — but they developed inside eggs, not a placenta.
quiz.objective: Distinguish oviparous, viviparous and ovoviviparous animals

quiz.text: Why does variation matter to a species?
options: It lets some individuals survive a change that kills the rest
It makes the animals look more interesting
It removes the need for a partner
quiz.explain: A population of clones shares every weakness. One disease that beats one of them beats all of them.

quiz.text: Asexual reproduction is faster than sexual reproduction.
quiz.explain: True, and it needs no partner. The cost is that there is no variation at all.
quiz.objective: Explain the difference between asexual and sexual reproduction

teacher.summary: Week 7 Science covers reproduction, matching the Term 1 weekly scope. The lesson is organised as a trade-off rather than as two lists: asexual reproduction is fast, cheap and needs no partner, and its single weakness — no variation — is what makes sexual reproduction worth its cost. The car card makes that concrete with a recall, which is the same failure mode as a disease sweeping a clone population. The flowerParts figure carries the plant half, because every exam question on it needs the diagram and no photograph shows the inside. Pollination and fertilisation are separated deliberately and tested twice, since treating them as one word is the most common error in the topic.
discussion: Ask why a species would bother with sexual reproduction when asexual is faster and needs no partner. Variation is the answer, and it is worth reaching rather than being told.
Ask him to point at a potato's eyes and say what they are. Vegetative propagation stops being abstract immediately.
Ask what pollination and fertilisation each mean, in his own words. If they come out as one thing, that is the gap.
Ask why siblings are different from each other. It is the same shuffle, one generation closer.
teacher.extension: Put a cutting from a plant in water and have him watch for roots over a fortnight. It is asexual reproduction happening on a windowsill, on his timescale.
misconceptions: 'Pollination and fertilisation are the same thing.' Pollination is pollen landing on a stigma. Fertilisation is the joining that happens later, in the ovary.
'Asexual reproduction only happens in plants.' Amoebae, hydra, starfish and some lizards all do it.
'The seed is the fruit.' The ovules become the seeds and the ovary around them becomes the fruit.
'Clones are stronger because they are identical.' They share every weakness, which is exactly why variation matters.
